commenti.body: I haven't seen a single one of his films, and given the kinda person he is, it's probably gonna stay that way. I don't really believe in separating art from the artist, because art is an extension of the artist, to understand one is to understand the other. That said, part of the human experience is being shitty, and I think it's limiting to ignore stuff just because it was made by someone shitty. But with Woody Allen, he's shitty *and* has a generally annoying demeanour so I find all of that offputting

I love woody Allen’s movies and after reading the case, I don’t think he did anything wrong. Sure, marrying his wife’s stepdaughter is weird but I don’t think he did anymore than that. 

Midnight in Paris is good but personally, I think he’s made far better films. I honestly think the movies he stars/acts in are by far his best films because he’s a comedic genius.

Yeah, you can’t really control how people respond to the art/artist thing. I’m a big fan of Allen and Polanski’s work so have certainly run into a few outraged people. Don’t try and convince them, they just went down a different road, let them go, it’s fine.

For people willing to engage with the movies, yes, there’s great stuff! Seen anything else of his?
The range of art that you consume must be absolutely tiny then
No, I just don't wanna watch Woody Allen films

If you are going to contradict your supposed principles regarding the interplay between aesthetics and ethics within a single paragraph, then it is better to skip the sanctimonious soapboxing bullshit and just say you find him annoying.
